_doc: Decision rules of the analysis (Sleuthline 2.0b). After the triage steps and after each investigation task, the program evaluates these rules and opens leads; each lead becomes a focused task of the agent. kind = finding: regular expressions on the text of a recorded finding (title, description, analysis, category, MITRE); all of regex_all must match. kind = timeline: regular expression on the description of the timeline and detections (data-driven, before any finding); skipped when every matching record is already cited by a finding. kind = ioc: a recorded IOC that appears in records not cited by any finding (entity graph). priority: high, medium, low. Placeholders of question: {finding_id} {finding_title} {hosts} {count} {sample_refs} {ioc_type} {ioc_value} {extra}. Source of truth: <repository>\pipeline\config\decision_rules.json.

rules.question: Finding {finding_id} ({finding_title}) shows a remote logon from an internal address. Which machine was the source, what ran there just before (outbound RDP / SMB / WinRM, the same account, the same tools), and was that machine compromised?
Finding {finding_id} ({finding_title}) points to password guessing. From which addresses, against which accounts, did a logon succeed afterwards, and what did that session do?

Where does the file or command used by the persistence of {finding_id} ({finding_title}) come from (download, copy, archive, dropper), what is its hash, where else does it appear (pivot on every host and in the capture), and when did it run?

For the command-and-control activity of {finding_id} ({finding_title}): which remote addresses and domains, seen on which hosts and in the capture, since when, which processes used them, and does the same binary (hash) exist elsewhere?

Finding {finding_id} ({finding_title}) indicates credential access. Were credentials actually taken (dump files, tools, handles to lsass, SAM / NTDS copies), which accounts had sessions on that host at the time, and were they used afterwards (logons on this or other hosts)?
Finding {finding_id} ({finding_title}) suggests the use of stolen authentication material. Which account and key material, from which host, and where was it used next?
For {finding_id} ({finding_title}): which service accounts were targeted, from which host and account, and were their credentials used afterwards?
Which machine and account launched the remote execution of {finding_id} ({finding_title}), what did it run on this host, and on which other hosts did the same happen?
Decode and follow the command of {finding_id} ({finding_title}): what was downloaded or executed, from where, and what happened next on that host?
For {finding_id} ({finding_title}): which account was created or given privileges, by whom, from where, and was it used afterwards (logons, hosts)?

What was the attacker hiding with the evasion of {finding_id} ({finding_title})? Review the activity on the same host in the window before it for actions it was meant to cover, and what remains despite it.
For {finding_id} ({finding_title}): how did the data leave (C2 sessions, cloud uploads, mail, removable media, RDP clipboard / drive), how much, when, and which files were concerned?
For {finding_id} ({finding_title}): which removable device, first and last connection, which user, and which files were copied to or from it? Distinguish the responder's own devices.
Scope of the impact of {finding_id} ({finding_title}): which files and hosts were encrypted or destroyed, when it started, which binary, how it was launched and from where.
Event logs were cleared ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): by whom, when, from which process, and what is missing around that time?
Recovery was inhibited ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): by which process and account, when, and what followed (encryption, wiping)?
Encoded PowerShell was run ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): decode it, then follow what it did (downloads, connections, files, persistence).

Directory replication rights were used ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): from which account and machine? A non-DC requester means DCSync: which accounts were exposed (krbtgt) and what followed?
Kerberos service tickets with RC4 were requested ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): Kerberoasting? Which requester, which service accounts, and were they used afterwards?
Members were added to security groups ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): which accounts, which groups (privileged?), by whom, and was it part of the incident?

Services were installed from an unusual location or with a command line ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): which binaries, installed by whom and from where (remote execution?), and what did they do?
Windows binaries were used to download or run remote content ({count} record(s), e.g. {sample_refs}): what was fetched, from where, and what ran next?
IOC {ioc_type} {ioc_value} appears in {extra} record(s) not cited by any finding (hosts {hosts}): what are they, and do they extend the incident (other hosts, other times)?
